cards.title: Where your donations actually come from (it isn't the homepage)
cards.headline: /reb-meirs-guarantee/ alone drove $430,401 — while many high-traffic article pages convert $0
cards.detail: Donation revenue is concentrated in a few funnels. The 'Reb Meir's Guarantee' page generated $430K; meanwhile high-traffic info pages (/download-app/ 1,977 sessions, how-to-write-shidduch-resume 1,190 sessions, parashas-hamon) convert at $0. 'The homepage makes the money' is an attribution artifact — the real pattern is funnel-page vs content-page.
cards.action: Port the proven donate mechanics from the Guarantee/homepage funnels onto the $0 high-traffic content cluster (10,000+ sessions / 6mo). Same articles, add the donation path.

cards.title: Mobile isn't broken — it converts BETTER and drives 71% of revenue
cards.headline: Mobile 11.96% vs desktop 9.65% conversion; mobile = $754,440 of $1,062,050 (71%)
cards.detail: Any 'rebuild mobile checkout' plan would risk 71% of revenue for a non-problem. The real underperformer is DESKTOP — it ranks ~7 positions deeper (page 2) on the same terms. Page speed (LCP ~4.7s) is still worth fixing as upside, not as a checkout emergency.
cards.action: Drop any mobile-checkout rebuild. Attack desktop page-2 rankings instead; keep page-speed as an upside lever, not a fire.

cards.title: 175 keywords are one nudge from a click windfall (positions 4-10)
cards.headline: 175 RMBH-owned queries rank 4-10 with sub-1% CTR — e.g. 'shidduch' 10,060 impr at #6, 'prayer for lost things' 5,548 at #5
cards.detail: These are pages you already own, sitting just below the click fold. A small rank gain here = a large click gain, far cheaper than new content. Prioritize donation-intent terms (prayer / branded / shidduch) over 'meaning/definition' queries that won't convert.
cards.action: Work the intent-weighted list top-down: internal links + on-page depth to push these from #4-10 into the top 3.

cards.title: 3-4x channel conversion gap, and returning donors convert 2x
cards.headline: PMax/Cross-network 23.2% vs Organic 6.4% vs Direct 7.3%; returning visitors 19.4% vs new 10.2% (34% of revenue)
cards.detail: Organic Social is effectively dead (3 donations/yr). Returning visitors are only 21-23% of sessions but drive 34% of revenue, concentrated in Email (33%) and Cross-network (31%). The retention channels are underexploited.
cards.action: Stop investing in Organic Social; grow the email list from article pages; expand retargeting/Cross-network audiences; scale PMax while watching incrementality.

cards.title: 300 finished articles are written but unpublished — earning $0
cards.headline: 12 hubs fully written but ZERO published (Refuah 48, Holidays 42, Middos 39…) = 300 ready articles, plus 98 more in proven hubs
cards.detail: 60% of the 502-article corpus is written but not live, producing no clicks and no donations. Proven hubs (Mourning, Tehillim, Educational) already rank page-1 with siblings locked. Publishing the backlog is the cheapest growth lever available.
cards.action: Publish proven hubs first (Mourning → Tehillim → Educational → Lifecycles → Parnassah → Shabbat), then whole dark silos starting Refuah & Health (48, highest intent) — after the Torah-citation QA gate. Don't trickle.

cards.title: Page speed — the exact one-click fixes (not just 'it's slow')
cards.headline: 41 render-blocking resources, a 730KiB hero PNG served TWICE (1.46MB redundant), and 2 DEAD Universal Analytics tags still loading
cards.detail: Mobile perf 46/100, LCP ~4.7s site-wide. Named causes: render-blocking CSS/JS (Salient 90KiB, Elementor 46KiB, salient-child CSS loaded twice, font-awesome 3x, 268KiB unused CSS); the hero PNG duplicated; and two dead UA tags (UA-218956708-1, UA-89597134-1, killed Jul 2023) plus a duplicate GTM container.
cards.action: Theme/plugin pass (WP Rocket / Perfmatters): inline critical CSS + defer the rest & jQuery; de-dup the 730KiB PNG → WebP with preload + fetchpriority on the hero; remove both dead UA tags and consolidate to one GTM container. ~500-900ms faster, ~1.5MB lighter, site-wide.

cards.title: /lost-object/ — your single biggest converter — is bleeding clicks
cards.headline: −2,308 clicks (−26%, 8,767→6,459); supporting queries slipped, e.g. 'bracha for lost items' #1.3→#6.1
cards.detail: This one flagship page is declining while the rest of the site grows — an isolated underperformer, not a site-wide drop. It answers the 'Amar Rabbi Binyamin' prayer-for-lost-objects searches that are core to Rabbi Meir Baal Haness.
cards.action: P0 content refresh: full Amar Rabbi Binyamin prayer (Hebrew + transliteration + English), FAQ schema, internal links from homepage/brand pages, fresh date + 2-3 links. Worth ~2,300 of your highest-converting clicks per 6 months.

cards.title: Slipping brand rankings carry an ~$18K price tag
cards.headline: Brand clicks −23% (impressions +24%); organic conversions −20%, organic revenue −21% ($85.3K→$67.1K)
cards.detail: RMBH is shown more but clicked less on its OWN brand terms — pushed below the top result. 'rabbi meir baal haness prayer' fell #1.1→#3.7 (−248 clicks, the single biggest loser); 'donate' #1.8→#22.7. GA4 confirms the revenue cost even though total organic sessions grew +11%.
cards.action: Eyeball the live SERPs for the core brand terms to see what now outranks RMBH (AI Overview vs competitor vs feature change), then reclaim #1 on the homepage + /lost-object/ and build a real /donate landing page.

cards.title: Rankings & visibility are soaring — but clicks are flat
cards.headline: Impressions +24% · avg position 9.7→7.6 · CTR 2.1%→1.6% · clicks -6%
cards.detail: Positions improved and impressions jumped, yet clicks barely moved — because CTR fell. That inversion (better rank, worse CTR) is the signature of Google AI Overviews / zero-click search answering informational and prayer queries directly.
cards.action: Win the AI-Overview citation (Goal 5), write titles/snippets that earn the click beyond the answer, and lean into intent queries (kvittel, donate) where a click is required.

cards.title: Top keywords that slipped out of their rankings
cards.headline: 10 high-value terms dropped rank — including brand, donation and lost-object queries that were #1
cards.detail: Compared over the last 3 full months versus the same period a year ago. These are not zero-click losses — the page actually fell in Google; the average improved overall only because new long-tail content masked these crown-term slips. This half is recoverable.
cards.action: Re-optimize these specific pages (freshness, internal links, content depth) to win back top 3 — prioritize the donation/brand terms first.

cards.title: The site is slow — especially on mobile
cards.headline: Avg mobile performance 65/100 · real-user load (LCP) ~4414ms — Google's "poor" zone (good is <2,500ms)
cards.detail: Real-user LCP is uniform across pages (3567–4617ms), so this is a site-wide template problem, not page-by-page. Slow load makes users bounce before the page renders — hurting CTR, conversion (the donation pages are among the slowest), and rankings.
cards.action: Fix the shared template once (image/font/script loading) to lift every page. Prioritize the homepage and the kvitel/donate pages.

cards.title: Does page speed correlate with the ranking drop? (partly, yes)
cards.headline: Correlation r = 0.18 across 8 key pages — slower pages tended to drop, faster pages rose
cards.detail: This is cross-sectional (one speed snapshot, n=8) so it's suggestive, not proof. We've now started logging speed monthly so the speed-vs-ranking relationship becomes a real time series you can watch.
cards.action: Treat speed as a site-wide ranking & conversion headwind worth fixing; re-measure the correlation monthly as the log builds.
